gaps.lead: She found it hard to understand the accent.
gaps.explanation: 'Have difficulty (in) doing' = find it hard to do.

gaps.lead: He spoke slowly because he wanted us to understand him.
gaps.explanation: so that + subject + would/could expresses purpose.

gaps.lead: He can't be in Spain — I saw him here this morning.
gaps.sentence: He ___ in Spain — I saw him this morning.
gaps.explanation: can't/cannot possibly be = it is impossible that he is.

gaps.lead: The journey was so tiring that we slept all day.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ that we slept all day.
gaps.explanation: so tiring (a journey) → such a tiring journey.

gaps.lead: The flat was too cramped for their three children.
gaps.sentence: The flat wasn't ___ their three children.
gaps.explanation: too cramped for = not spacious enough for.

gaps.lead: It was a mistake not to write the telephone number down.
gaps.sentence: I should ___ writing down the telephone number.
gaps.hint: make a point of doing = be sure to do
gaps.explanation: Regret about an omitted action: 'should have made a point of writing it down'.

gaps.lead: Pay claims must be submitted before the end of the month.
gaps.sentence: You have ___ your pay claims before the end of the month.
gaps.explanation: 'Must be submitted' becomes 'you have to put in your claims'.

gaps.lead: I haven't seen a better film this year.
gaps.sentence: This is ___ I've seen this year.
gaps.explanation: I haven't seen a better film = this is the best film (that) I've seen.
